The supplied timing data has no phase-level breakdown that explains why the longest compute-bound experiment was slow.

The point-in-time GPU snapshot is not correlated with compute-bound task windows, and the supplied data does not establish whether any multi-model workload loaded models concurrently or missed DualGPURunner dispatch.
improvements_suggested: Record direct task start and end timestamps, phase timers, and task-window GPU utilization for every compute-bound experiment.
Add checkpoint/resume and a configurable early feasibility cutoff to the Live ARC budget-2000 harness so long runs emit actionable intermediate evidence.
Record model-concurrency and runner-dispatch receipts, selecting DualGPURunner only when at least two models are loaded in parallel.

meta_reflection: The reconstruction identifies where elapsed time concentrated but cannot explain the internal cause. Task-window telemetry and runner-dispatch receipts are required before a nonzero time-savings estimate can be supported.
